- Yellowing (chlorosis) on the upper/top portion
- Brown necrotic spots scattered on the yellowed area
- Marginal browning and curling at the leaf tip
- Lower portion still green
- No obvious fungal growth visible

Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Leaf_Mold, Early_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch. Let me view references one at a time.
Bacterial Canker shows strong marginal scorch all around edges. The test image has more diffuse upper yellowing. Let me check Leaf Mold.
Leaf Mold shows patchy yellowing on the upper surface, somewhat similar. Now checking Early Blight.
Early Blight shows severe brown wilting, doesn't match well. Let me check Septoria Leaf Blotch.
Septoria shows small dark spots on yellowing leaf - somewhat similar but spots are smaller/more numerous than test image. Let me check Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.
TSWV shows purple/bronze spotting - doesn't match. Let me check Late Blight.
Microscopic image not useful. Let me check Verticillium Wilt (yellowing/wilting pattern) as a candidate.
Verticillium shows interveinal yellowing but on a different host. Let me use my last view to compare with Septoria Leaf Blotch more closely.

| Class | Visual Match |
|---|---|
| Bacterial Canker | Heavy marginal scorch all around - doesn't match |
| Leaf Mold (CDDM_1006) | Patchy yellowing on upper surface - somewhat similar but no distinct spots |
| Early Blight | Severe widespread browning - doesn't match |
| Septoria Leaf Blotch (CDDM_1006) | Yellowing leaf with scattered dark spots - **most similar** |
| Septoria Leaf Blotch (CDDM_1035) | Mostly green with tiny spots - less similar |
| TSWV | Purple/bronze spotting - doesn't match |
| Late Blight | Microscopic reference - not useful |
| Verticillium Wilt | Interveinal yellowing - somewhat similar pattern |

The test image shows a tomato leaf with diffuse yellowing on the upper/distal half, scattered brown necrotic spots within the yellow zone, and tip die-back at the margin. The Septoria Leaf Blotch reference (CDDM_1006) was the closest match: overall leaf yellowing with dark spots scattered through the tissue. The asymmetric pattern (tip/upper margin yellowing while leaf base stays green) is consistent with Septoria progression.
